Precious Metals Quarterly 1Q2007 Platinum # Platinum ## Recent trends Platinum maintained a gentle up-trend from mid-December through to early March, primarily in response to supply-side news. A sell-off in the global equity and commodities markets saw platinum fall by almost 7% to a low of $1,165/oz on 5 March, but the correction was shortlived. The price is now eyeing the $1,250/oz level on the back of a shortage of platinum sponge that was first reported in mid-March. This shortage remains today (early April), with sponge trading at a premium to Zurich ingot by up to $3/oz. Rumours regarding the introduction of an exchange-traded fund in platinum again materialised, but while this did provide some support to prices, there was not the stratospheric reaction that we saw last November. CRU maintains its view that an ETF would be unlikely to receive regulatory approval given the strong opposition it would face. - While the market was quiet towards the end of 2006, physical demand in Asia, and to a lesser extent in Europe, provided a fillip to prices in the first half of January. Industrial demand has been somewhat lacklustre since platinum broke through $1,200/oz. - Fresh investment money flowing into gold spilled over into the platinum market in February, taking the price higher. Latest CFTC data shows that the net non-commercial long position on NYMEX increased to 5,553 contracts (8.6 tonnes) on 27 March, the highest level for more than thirteen months. Platinum continues to attract investors with news underlining its sound fundamental outlook. A new law was passed in Germany at the end of March whereby owners of older diesel vehicles who retrofit particulate filters will be offered a oneoff rebate on annual road tax of about €330. Vehicles not fitted with a filter and that fail to meet EU emissions standards will incur a €25/year increase in excise duty. At the same time, the Platinum Guild International launched its jewellery marketing campaign in Japan and forecasts sales of about ¥64 billion in the first year alone. - In mid-December, Lonmin announced that it had closed its Number One furnace for 30 days, however, on moving into the New Year it emerged that a rebuild was opted for and this was forecast to take more than three months to complete. Technical issues at a South Africanbased power provider caused minor problems for local miners Anglo- and Impala Platinum towards the end of January, but also raised concerns over the reliability of future power supply. Almost simultaneously, workers at South Africa’s Modikwa mine began industrial action over working conditions and pay, which was not resolved until 19 February, and resulted in the loss of more than 3,400oz of platinum. ##### Vehicle production set for continued growth Pt demand in the autocat sector is forecast to grow by an annual average of 4.6% until 2011. Much of this grow th stems from Asia, w hich seems to be occurring at the expense of the North American and West European vehicle markets. Japanese car production increased by almost 8% in 2006 as domestic manufacturers continued to make inroads (primarily) into the North American market. JD Pow er forecasts that pricing pressure and other competitive factors from the likes of Honda and Toyota is likely to continue in the short-term. Furthermore, expansions in European manufacturing capacity is unlikely to be paralleled by capacity utilisation, how ever, rising diesel market share w ill help maintain platinum offtake. Precious Metals Quarterly 1Q2007 Platinum 31 ## Forecast update: strength in autocatalyst sector to offset weaker jewellery demand Since the platinum price spiked at an all-time record high of $1,355/oz in nominal terms last November, platinum has made steady gains from the low $1,100’s/oz to trade around the $1,250s at the end of 2007 Q1 - with just one correction that temporarily set the market back. This quarter we take a look at some of the developments in the two major offtake sectors for platinum that could impact demand over the next couple of years. #### **Autocatalysts** The stage is set for the market share of diesel-engine vehicles to increase in the USA. In January, President Bush outlined the latest energy plan for the country, which calls for a 20% reduction in petrol consumption over the next decade. CRU forecasts that oil prices will remain at elevated levels over the forecast period, and combined with ongoing concerns over the country’s energy independence, this provides further incentive for the switch to diesel fuel. Also, the successful introduction of the new government policy requiring the use of low sulphur (<15ppm) diesel fuel in October 2006 has meant that auto manufacturers are expecting a surge in diesel vehicle sales. Domestic manufacturers are preparing to roll out light-duty diesel trucks for 2009, as by 2010 all fuel is required to be low sulphur. The light vehicle market in the USA as a whole is not faring particularly well with domestic manufacturers facing intense competition from overseas producers – namely Japan (see _Platinum Storyboard_ ). Car assembly is expected to rema

in virtually unchanged over the forecast period at 4.19 million units in 2011, compared with 4.178 million units this year. However, in 2007, new federal emission standards for heavy-duty vehicles (truck and bus engines) come into force. These focus on reducing NOx emissions from 4.0 to 0.2g/bhp.hr and particulate matter (PM) from 0.005 to 0.001g/bhp.hr (see Table 7), which can be met initially through engine modifications and management. However, new models will require ##### CRU forecasts that oil will remain at elevated prices $/bbl

the fitment of DOC (diesel oxidation catalyst) and/or CSF (catalysed soot filter) technology to meet PM limits, and SCR (selective catalytic reduction) technology to comply with NOx limits over the next four years. As JD Power forecasts that HDV production in the USA will increase by about 18% between 2007 and 2011 (and bearing in mind that autocatalysts fitted in HDV’s require heavier PGM loadings than light-duty vehicles) we therefore estimate that platinum usage in autocats in North America will increase by 11.8% to just under 1.1Moz in 2011. 32 Precious Metals Quarterly 1Q2007 Platinum Johnson Matthey recently reported that in 2006, over 50% of new cars registered in the EU (excluding new member countries) were diesel-powered. The construction of new diesel refineries in Europe and the Middle East reflects the growth in demand for this fuel in Western Europe over the past five or so years. However, according to JD Power, annual growth in ##### Johnson Matthey and Umicore are the current leading autocatalyst manufacturers BASF Johnson Matthey Umicore Other

More significant for platinum offake over the forecast period therefore is the introduction of Euro V and Euro VI legislation, which will require auto manufacturers to fit catalysed diesel particulate filters (DPFs) and the use of SCR technology will become more widespread. The NOx and HC limit for light-duty diesel vehicles under Euro V legislation has been revised downwards since the last _Precious Metals Quarterly_ , while standards for other pollutants have remained unchanged (see Table 6). In the light-duty vehicle sector, Euro V legislation (to be introduced in mid-2008) will reduce NOx limits to 0.06g/km for petrol engines and to 0.18g/km for diesel engines. PM limits are set at 0g/km and 0.005g/km respectively. Continued strong growth in Asian vehicle manufacturing will very likely offset weakness in the European and North American markets. Adding to this is the introduction of new legislation for light, medium and heavy-duty diesel vehicles in Japan in 2009, which (as in E

urope) target specifically NOx and PM emissions (see Table 8) and the possible implementation of a new policy in Seoul.  As part of plans to improve air quality in the city, the Seoul Metropolitan Government is aiming to ensure that all older diesel-powered trucks (those over seven years old) that weigh over 3.5t are fitted with diesel particulate filters by the end of 2008.  Drivers who fail to comply could incur penalty charges.  In the light truck sector, Korea manufactured more than 220,000 units in 2006 and this figure could rise by 46% over the net four years. 

#### **Jewellery** 

Jewellery is the one component of demand that has really been pressurised by the high and volatile prices, with consumers at the more price-sensitive fashion end turning to white gold and palladium.  Even in Europe, one of the most price-inelastic regions for platinum jewellery offtake (having remained between 190-195koz from 2003 to 2005, during which time the platinum price increased by 30%), demand contracted by some 20koz in 2006. 

CRU expects jewellery demand to remain weak in 2007 on the back of further price appreciation, and we could even see offtake in China, which accounts for about 45% of global platinum jewellery demand, fall by a similar percentage this year as in 2006.  This will, in part, depend on the extent to which manufacturers and retailers take advantage of any price dips to restock inventories following recycling activities.  However, a plan to raise consumption tax on 

Precious Metals Quarterly 1Q2007    Platinum 

33 

luxury goods in China, including jewellery, could offset on new purchases of the metal for restocking purposes. 

On the other side of the coin, platinum’s high price really enforces its image as a luxury metal and for this reason offtake in the bridal or high-end sector is expected to remain fairly buoyant in most markets (providing we do not see price spikes of the magnitude experienced in November 2006).  Not all regions are immune though - reports indicate that substitution occurred in the USA bridal sector in 2006, and we see no reason for this not to continue this year. 

Demand for platinum jewellery in India grew by 30% in 2006, with offtake notably improving (competing with gold) during the Indian wedding season, which began in midJanuary.  Both traditional and modern jewellers saw significant growth in demand for the metal during the festive season – previously considered an auspicious gold buying occasion.  Platinum jewellery was introduced into this country at prices of more than $1,200/oz.  The Platinum Guild International (PGI) recently launched its ‘Thanks Days Platinum’ marketing campaign in Japan.  A new range of platinum and diamond jewellery is being marketed in about 1,200 jewellery stores initially (in up to 2,000 stores by the 2008), and through television and print media advertisements.  The PGI is targeting older consumers with a higher disposable income and forecasts sales of ¥64 billion (US$544

million) in the first year. Should the campaign prove successful, as it had in India, the introduction of platinum at prices in the mid$1,200s/oz is a very positive development for future platinum offtake in the jewellery sector, which, for the fourth consecutive year, has been on a downward trend. Looking further ahead, demand for platinum in the jewellery sector is expected to increase again from 2008 as surplus in the market begins to weigh on prices. However, we do not see demand returning to anywhere near pre-2004 levels within the time frame of our forecast period. #### **Forecast balance and prices** ##### Jewellery demand further dampened by high and volatile prices in 2006 2,500

For our estimate of the final balance in the platinum market in 2006, we previously forecast that the market would be in marginal surplus by about 17,000oz. However, recently released trade data for the full year 2006 shows that Russian annual derived shipments from stock were far lower than expected. Notably imports into Switzerland, Japan, the USA, China and Hong Kong were all lower (in some cases much lower) compared with previous years. Shipments from stock were only slightly more than half that recorded in 2005, yet total Russian production was likely only down by about 20koz. Therefore, while the basic balance for 2006 (excluding stock movements) shows the market was in surplus by about 90koz, the final balance comes in at a deficit of about 330koz. 34 Precious Metals Quarterly 1Q2007 Platinum CRU expects the platinum market to move into surplus by more than 100koz from 2008, mostly on the back of mine expansions in South Africa, but also through secondary recovery with the increased availability of platinum-bearing spent autocatalysts. Demand for the metal will continue to grow over the forecast period driven by offtake in the autocatalyst sector, which will offset weakness in the jewellery sector in the short-term We are forecasting a long-term average platinum price of $1,015/oz.
